sections.heading: 1.1 Uniform Circular Motion & Centripetal Acceleration
sections.content: Uniform Circular Motion (UCM) is the motion of a particle along the circumference of a circle with constant speed. The acceleration directed towards the center along the radius is centripetal acceleration ac = v²/r = ω²r.
keyPoints: Linear velocity is always tangential: v = r · ω
Centripetal force is real: F = m · v² / r = m · ω² · r
Centrifugal force is a pseudo force experienced in a rotating non-inertial frame
sections.formula: v_max = √(μ_s · r · g) (on unbanked circular road)

sections.heading: 1.2 Banking of Roads
sections.content: To avoid reliance on friction alone, curved roads are banked at an angle θ with the horizontal. At the optimum speed, neither wear nor tear occurs.
keyPoints: Optimum speed without friction: v = √(r · g · tan θ)
Maximum safe speed with friction: v_max = √[r · g · (μ + tan θ) / (1 - μ · tan θ)]
Minimum safe speed: v_min = √[r · g · (tan θ - μ) / (1 + μ · tan θ)]

sections.heading: 1.3 Moment of Inertia (M.I.) & Radius of Gyration
sections.content: Moment of inertia is the rotational analogue of mass. It depends on the mass distribution about the given axis of rotation: I = ∑ m_i · r_i².
keyPoints: Radius of gyration K: I = M · K²
Theorem of Parallel Axes: I_O = I_C + M · h²
Theorem of Perpendicular Axes: I_Z = I_X + I_Y (for planar lamina)
M.I. of Ring: I = M · R²
M.I. of Uniform Disc: I = ½ · M · R²
M.I. of Solid Sphere: I = (2/5) · M · R²
sections.formula: I = M · K² ; I_O = I_C + M · h²

sections.heading: 1.4 Rolling Motion on an Inclined Plane
sections.content: A body rolling without slipping possesses both translational and rotational kinetic energy: E_total = ½ M v² + ½ I ω² = ½ M v² (1 + K² / R²).
keyPoints: Acceleration down incline: a = (g · sin θ) / (1 + K² / R²)
Velocity at bottom: v = √[ (2 · g · h) / (1 + K² / R²) ]
Solid cylinder / disc: K²/R² = 1/2
Solid sphere: K²/R² = 2/5 (reaches bottom fastest)

sections.heading: 4.1 First Law of Thermodynamics
sections.content: Energy can neither be created nor destroyed, although it may be converted from one form to another: ΔU = q + w. For pressure-volume work: w = -P_ext · ΔV.
keyPoints: Work done in isothermal reversible expansion: W_max = -2.303 · n · R · T · log₁₀(V₂ / V₁)
Isochoric process (ΔV = 0): q_v = ΔU
Isobaric process (constant P): q_p = ΔH = ΔU + P · ΔV
sections.formula: W_max = -2.303 n R T log₁₀(P₁ / P₂)

sections.heading: 4.2 Enthalpy & Hess Law of Constant Heat Summation
sections.content: Enthalpy H is the sum of internal energy and PV energy. Hess Law states that the overall enthalpy change for a chemical reaction is independent of the pathway taken.
keyPoints: ΔH = ΔU + Δn_g · R · T (where Δn_g = moles of gaseous products - moles of gaseous reactants)
If Δn_g = 0, then ΔH = ΔU

sections.heading: 4.3 Second Law, Entropy & Gibbs Free Energy
sections.content: Total entropy of universe always increases in a spontaneous process. Gibbs free energy G = H - TS determines spontaneity under constant T and P.
keyPoints: ΔG = ΔH - T · ΔS
If ΔG < 0: Process is spontaneous
If ΔG = 0: System is at equilibrium (ΔG° = -2.303 · R · T · log₁₀ K)
If ΔG > 0: Process is non-spontaneous
sections.formula: ΔG = ΔH - TΔS ; ΔG° = -RT ln K

sections.heading: 5.1 Derivative of Composite Functions (Chain Rule)
sections.content: If y = f(u) is a differentiable function of u and u = g(x) is a differentiable function of x, then dy/dx = (dy/du) · (du/dx).
keyPoints: d/dx [f(x)]ⁿ = n · [f(x)]ⁿ⁻¹ · f'(x)
d/dx [sin(f(x))] = cos(f(x)) · f'(x)

sections.heading: 5.2 Logarithmic & Parametric Differentiation
sections.content: When functions are of the form [f(x)]^(g(x)) or involve complex products and quotients, taking natural logarithms simplifies differentiation. For x = f(t) and y = g(t), dy/dx = (dy/dt) / (dx/dt).
keyPoints: y = x^x ⇒ ln y = x ln x ⇒ dy/dx = x^x (1 + ln x)
d²y/dx² = d/dt(dy/dx) · (dt/dx)

sections.heading: 1.1 Microsporogenesis & Pollen Grain Structure
sections.content: Microsporangium contains sporogenous tissue that undergoes meiosis to produce haploid microspores (pollen grains). Anther consists of four wall layers: Epidermis, Endothecium, Middle layers, and Tapetum (nutritive).
keyPoints: Tapetum nourishes developing microspores and secretes callase and sporopollenin
Exine made of Sporopollenin (most resistant organic material known)
Intine is thin, pectin-cellulose layer
sections.formula: 1 Microspore Mother Cell (2n) → 4 functional pollen grains (n)

sections.heading: 1.2 Double Fertilization & Endosperm Formation
sections.content: Unique to angiosperms: One male gamete fuses with egg cell (Syngamy → 2n Zygote), second male gamete fuses with diploid secondary nucleus (Triple fusion → 3n Primary Endosperm Nucleus - PEN).
keyPoints: Syngamy: n + n → 2n Embryo
Triple Fusion: n + 2n → 3n Endosperm
Types of endosperm: Nuclear (coconut water), Cellular, and Helobial

formulas.name: Perpendicular Axes Theorem
formulas.note: Valid strictly for planar 2D laminar bodies

formulas.name: Torque & Angular Momentum
formulas.formula: τ = I · α ; L = I · ω
formulas.note: Conservation of angular momentum if τ_ext = 0

formulas.name: Total Kinetic Energy in Rolling
formulas.formula: E_k = ½ M v² (1 + K² / R²)

keyReactionsOrLaws: Law of Conservation of Angular Momentum: If external torque τ_ext = 0, then L = I · ω = Constant.
Theorem of Parallel Axes applies to any rigid 3D body of mass M.
Theorem of Perpendicular Axes applies only to 2D laminar objects (discs, rings, plates).
tips: In vertical circular motion: Velocity at top = √(rg), Velocity at bottom = √(5rg), Tension difference = 6mg.
For rolling without slipping, solid sphere has least (1 + K²/R²) = 1.4, so it accelerates fastest down an incline.

keyReactionsOrLaws: First Law of Thermodynamics: ΔU = q + w (IUPAC: work done ON system is positive).
Hess Law of Constant Heat Summation: Heat change is independent of the intermediate steps.

formulas.name: Pollen grains produced
formulas.formula: P = 4 × Number of Microspore Mother Cells

keyReactionsOrLaws: Anatropous ovule is the most common type in angiosperms (inverted ovule with micropyle facing down).
7-celled, 8-nucleate female gametophyte: 3 Antipodals, 2 Synergids, 1 Egg cell, 1 Central cell (2 polar nuclei).
Entomophily (insect pollination): Sticky, spiny, scented pollen grains.
Anemophily (wind pollination): Dry, light, non-sticky pollen produced in vast quantities.
tips: Double fertilization was discovered by S.G. Nawaschin in Lilium and Fritillaria.

questions.questionText: A car is negotiating a curved unbanked road of radius 40 m. If the coefficient of static friction between the tires and road is 0.4, the maximum speed with which the car can take the turn safely is (take g = 9.8 m/s²):
questions.solution: For an unbanked circular road, maximum safe speed v_max = √(μ_s · r · g). Here μ_s = 0.4, r = 40 m, g = 9.8 m/s². v_max = √(0.4 × 40 × 9.8) = √(156.8) ≈ 12.52 m/s. Hence Option B is correct.

questions.questionText: The ratio of the radius of gyration of a uniform circular disc about its diameter to that about an axis perpendicular to its plane passing through its center is:
questions.solution: M.I. of disc about perpendicular axis passing through center is I_z = ½ M R², so K_z = R / √2. M.I. of disc about diameter (by perpendicular axis theorem I_z = 2 I_d) is I_d = ¼ M R², so K_d = R / 2. Therefore, K_d / K_z = (R / 2) / (R / √2) = √2 / 2 = 1 / √2. Hence Option A is correct.

questions.questionText: A body rolls down an inclined plane without slipping. If the ratio of rotational kinetic energy to translational kinetic energy is 2/5, the body is a:
questions.solution: Rotational K.E. = ½ I ω² = ½ (M K²) (v/R)² = ½ M v² (K²/R²). Translational K.E. = ½ M v². The ratio is (Rotational K.E. / Translational K.E.) = K² / R². Since K² / R² = 2/5, the body is a Solid Sphere. Hence Option C is correct.

questions.questionText: A small body of mass m is tied to a string of length L and rotated in a vertical circle. The minimum tension in the string during complete circular motion is zero. The tension at the lowest point of the trajectory will be:
questions.solution: For complete vertical circular motion, tension at highest point T_top = m v_top² / L - mg. Setting T_top = 0 gives v_top = √(gL). By conservation of energy, v_bottom² = v_top² + 2g(2L) = 5gL. At the lowest point, tension T_bottom = m v_bottom² / L + mg = 5mg + mg = 6mg. Tension difference T_bottom - T_top = 6mg. Hence Option D is correct.

questions.questionText: When a detergent is dissolved in water, the surface tension of the liquid:
questions.solution: Detergents and surfactants weaken the cohesive intermolecular forces between water molecules at the surface, thereby significantly decreasing the surface tension. Hence Option B is correct.

questions.questionText: For the reaction: N₂(g) + 3 H₂(g) → 2 NH₃(g) at 298 K, which of the following statements is correct regarding ΔH and ΔU?
questions.solution: Formula: ΔH = ΔU + Δn_g · R · T. Here Δn_g = moles of gaseous products - moles of gaseous reactants = 2 - (1 + 3) = -2. Thus ΔH = ΔU - 2RT. Since 2RT > 0, ΔH is less than ΔU (ΔH < ΔU). Hence Option C is correct.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an intensive property?
questions.solution: An intensive property is independent of the amount of substance present in the system. Refractive index, density, and temperature are intensive properties. Mass, volume, and internal energy depend on the quantity of matter and are extensive properties. Hence Option C is correct.

questions.questionText: A metal crystallizes in a body-centered cubic (BCC) lattice with edge length 300 pm. The radius of the metal atom is:
questions.solution: In BCC lattice: 4r = √3 · a ⇒ r = (√3 / 4) · a. Given a = 300 pm: r = (1.732 / 4) × 300 = 0.433 × 300 = 129.9 pm. Hence Option A is correct.

questions.questionText: Which of the following 0.1 M aqueous solutions will exhibit the highest boiling point elevation?
questions.solution: ΔT_b = i · K_b · m. The solution with highest vant Hoff factor i has the highest boiling point elevation. For Glucose i = 1; for NaCl i = 2; for CaCl₂ i = 3; for Al₂(SO₄)₃ i = 2 + 3 = 5. Therefore, Al₂(SO₄)₃ has highest ΔT_b. Hence Option D is correct.

questions.questionText: The contrapositive of the statement "If a number is divisible by 9, then it is divisible by 3" is:

options.text: If a number is divisible by 3, then it is divisible by 9.
If a number is not divisible by 9, then it is not divisible by 3.
If a number is not divisible by 3, then it is not divisible by 9.
A number is divisible by 9 if and only if it is divisible by 3.

questions.solution: The contrapositive of conditional proposition p → q is ~q → ~p. Here p: "a number is divisible by 9", q: "it is divisible by 3". Thus ~q → ~p: "If a number is not divisible by 3, then it is not divisible by 9". Hence Option C is correct.

questions.questionText: If y = tan⁻¹ [ (cos x - sin x) / (cos x + sin x) ], then dy/dx is equal to:
questions.solution: Dividing numerator and denominator inside bracket by cos x: (1 - tan x) / (1 + tan x) = tan(π/4 - x). Hence y = tan⁻¹[tan(π/4 - x)] = π/4 - x. Differentiating with respect to x: dy/dx = 0 - 1 = -1. Hence Option B is correct.

questions.questionText: If A is a 3 × 3 non-singular matrix such that |A| = 4, then the value of |adj(A)| is:
questions.solution: Property of adjoint: |adj(A)| = |A|ⁿ⁻¹, where n is the order of square matrix A. Here n = 3 and |A| = 4. Therefore |adj(A)| = 4^(3 - 1) = 4² = 16. Hence Option B is correct.

questions.questionText: The value of the definite integral ∫₀^(π/2) [ sin³ x / (sin³ x + cos³ x) ] dx is:
questions.solution: Let I = ∫₀^(π/2) [sin³ x / (sin³ x + cos³ x)] dx ...(1). By property ∫₀^a f(x) dx = ∫₀^a f(a - x) dx, replacing x by (π/2 - x) gives: I = ∫₀^(π/2) [cos³ x / (cos³ x + sin³ x)] dx ...(2). Adding (1) and (2): 2I = ∫₀^(π/2) 1 dx = [x]₀^(π/2) = π/2 ⇒ I = π/4. Hence Option C is correct.

questions.questionText: In angiosperms, the ploidy level of the Primary Endosperm Nucleus (PEN) after double fertilization is:
questions.solution: In double fertilization, triple fusion occurs when one haploid male gamete (n) fuses with the diploid secondary nucleus (2n), giving rise to a triploid (3n) Primary Endosperm Nucleus (PEN). Hence Option C is correct.

questions.questionText: During transcription in prokaryotes, which enzyme subunit is responsible for the specific recognition of the promoter sequence?
questions.solution: The RNA polymerase holoenzyme in prokaryotes consists of the core enzyme (α₂ββ'ω) and the sigma (σ) initiation factor. Sigma factor specifically recognizes the promoter sequence (-10 Pribnow box and -35 region) to initiate transcription. Hence Option B is correct.

questions.questionText: The pacemaker of the human heart which generates rhythmic action potentials is:
questions.solution: The Sinoatrial Node (SA Node) located in the upper right wall of the right atrium generates action potentials at the highest rate (approx. 72 beats/min) and acts as the natural pacemaker of the heart. Hence Option C is correct.

questions.questionText: When a red-flowered Mirabilis jalapa plant is crossed with a white-flowered plant, the F1 offspring produce pink flowers. This phenomenon demonstrates:
questions.solution: In 4 O'clock plant (Mirabilis jalapa), neither allele is completely dominant over the other. The heterozygous condition (Rr) displays an intermediate phenotype (pink), which is classic Incomplete Dominance with a phenotypic and genotypic ratio of 1:2:1. Hence Option B is correct.

questions.questionText: The dimensional formula of surface tension is:
questions.modelSolution: Surface tension T = Force / Length. Dimensions of Force = [M¹ L¹ T⁻²]. Dimensions of Length = [L¹]. Thus [T] = [M¹ L¹ T⁻²] / [L¹] = [M¹ L⁰ T⁻²].

questions.section: Section B - Very Short Answer Type
questions.questionText: State any two conditions for steady interference pattern.
questions.modelSolution: Conditions: (1) The two sources of light must be coherent (constant phase difference). (2) The two interfering waves must be monochromatic (single wavelength). (3) The two sources should be narrow and close to each other.

questions.section: Section C - Short Answer Type II
questions.questionText: Derive an expression for the maximum safe speed of a vehicle on a banked circular road without considering friction.
questions.modelSolution: Let m be mass of vehicle, r be radius of curved road, θ be angle of banking. The normal reaction N resolves into two components: N cos θ = mg (balances weight) and N sin θ = m v² / r (provides centripetal force). Dividing: (N sin θ) / (N cos θ) = (m v² / r) / (mg) ⇒ tan θ = v² / (rg) ⇒ v = √(rg tan θ).

questions.questionText: The coordination number of atoms in a face-centered cubic (FCC) unit cell is:
questions.modelSolution: In an FCC (cubic close-packed) lattice, each sphere touches 12 neighboring spheres (6 in its own plane, 3 in plane above, 3 in plane below). Coordination number = 12.

questions.questionText: Define buffer solution. State one biological example of buffer system.
questions.correctAnswer: Resists change in pH on addition of small amounts of acid/base
questions.modelSolution: A buffer solution is defined as a solution which resists drastic changes in its pH value upon the addition of small amounts of strong acid or strong base. Biological example: Carbonic acid-bicarbonate buffer system (H₂CO₃ / HCO₃⁻) in human blood maintaining pH around 7.4.

questions.questionText: Distinguish between SN1 and SN2 reaction mechanisms with respect to kinetics and stereochemistry.
questions.correctAnswer: First order vs Second order; Racemization vs Inversion
questions.modelSolution: SN1: Unimolecular (Rate = k[R-X]), two-step mechanism via carbocation intermediate, leads to partial racemization. SN2: Bimolecular (Rate = k[R-X][Nu⁻]), single-step concerted mechanism via transition state, leads to 100% Walden inversion of configuration.

questions.questionText: The work done in blowing a soap bubble from radius R to 2R having surface tension T is:
questions.modelSolution: Soap bubble has two free surfaces. Initial area A₁ = 2 × 4π R² = 8π R². Final area A₂ = 2 × 4π (2R)² = 32π R². Increase in surface area ΔA = A₂ - A₁ = 32π R² - 8π R² = 24π R². Work done W = T × ΔA = 24 π R² T.

questions.questionText: The general solution of differential equation dy/dx + y tan x = sec x is:
options: y sec x = tan x + c
y tan x = sec x + c
y cos x = sin x + c
y sin x = cos x + c
questions.correctAnswer: Option A: y sec x = tan x + c
questions.modelSolution: This is a linear differential equation: P = tan x, Q = sec x. Integrating Factor IF = e^(∫ tan x dx) = e^(ln sec x) = sec x. General solution: y · (IF) = ∫ Q · (IF) dx + c ⇒ y · sec x = ∫ sec² x dx + c ⇒ y sec x = tan x + c.
